newsitem.title: TAIWAN: EARLY TAIWAN DOLLAR RISES ON TIGHT LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: EARLY TAIWAN DOLLAR RISES ON TIGHT LIQUIDITY.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar edged slightly firmer against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday due to the banking system's liquidity squeeze and the central bank's clear attempt to smooth the recent local currency fall, dealers said.
After 30 minutes at 0130 GMT, the local unit was at T$28.646 against Wednesday's T$28.656 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a light US$9 million.
On Wednesday, the overnight interbank rate finished at 8.748 percent against Tuesday's 7.784 end.
"Tight Taiwan dollar liquidity is a concern. But more importantly, the central bank's attitude prevents the market from making any drastic moves," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said the central bank would allow a slow and gradual Taiwan dollar slide, but it had intervened to smooth the local unit's fall in recent sessions.
A range of T$28.60-70 was seen for Thursday.
